Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear matrix. Quick answers below, and I attached a short SCCs summary and a draft UK addendum for your legal review.

1) Swiss fallback: yes, we support routing to Swiss-hosted inference nodes as an operational fallback. The routing policy we recommend is: primary EU cluster (Frankfurt) -> fallback Swiss cluster (Zurich) when UK addendum or specific residency constraints block the primary path. That fallback is enforced at the smart-routing layer and visible in our Console per-request logs.

2) UK addendum vs UK IDTA: for most contracts the addendum + TIA/DTIA packet is sufficient to satisfy procurement and external counsel if the TIA covers the operational safeguards. For high-risk health data OrchardHealth handles, some legal teams prefer full IDTA execution. We can support either; procurement option A: addendum + TIA (faster), option B: full IDTA (longer, stronger record).

3) Subprocessors and custody: current subprocessors for EU->CH routing are listed in the attached spreadsheet. Short summary:
- Primary compute: Redwood-managed GPU fleet in eu-central (Redwood infra team)
- Swiss fallback: Dedicated Swiss nodes operated by our partner Databox AG (access-limited)
- KMS/HSM: customer key material can be kept in your KMS (we support bring-your-own KMS via KMS-HSM integration). By default, transit logs and tokenization keys are stored in our EU KMS; for customers requiring Swiss custody we can integrate with Databox HSM for key wrapping at rest.

Next steps: Laura can run a quick tech note on KMS/HSM flows and Marcus can provide the subprocessor CSV with dates. I can also generate a DocuSign packet for addendum vs IDTA if you confirm preferred path.
